Are we about to see an early run on edge rushers in the NFL draft? ESPN draft analyst Jordan Reed tells us why it could happen. We'll build the perfect linebacker. Jordan will also make a case [music] for a trade up for the Jets in round one and will deliver a special two-round mock draft. Now boarding begins in three, two, one. Let's bring in ESPN NFL draft analyst Jordan Reed. Jordan, so great to see you once again. How big of an opportunity is this for the New York Jets to bring in some building blocks for this franchise considering their draft capital over the next two years? 19 picks in all, five in the first round over the next two drafts and eight in the first and second rounds combined. Well, it's huge. Whenever you have that amount of draft capital, it creates flexibility, which is what Aaron Glenn and Darren Moji want just because you're attempting to lay the foundation of this Jets roster that has already started bringing in a ton of better agency already. So now you want to sprinkle in those young players now they have a lot of opportunities with four picks in the first 44 picks. Excuse me, four picks inside of the first 44 picks, you have an opportunity to really lay the foundation of these players. Do you anticipate a run on edges there at the top of the draft because the consensus right now, Fernando Mendoza out of Indiana goes one to the Raiders. Could we see edges go two, three, four? I think we could and you talk about somebody like Arval Reese out of Ohio State and even David Bailey out of Texas Tech and also Ruben Bain out of Miami. I think those are your clear three edge rushers that could go off of the board consecutively. Now it's going to be really interesting to see which one the Jets do take at two. There's a clear need for them to rush the passer and whether it's Reese, Bailey, or Bain, they're going to have an opportunity to really continue to lay that foundation with a foundational piece with any one of those three players. Great transition right there. The Jets sitting there at number two overall. Uh let's do wheels up, wheels down as far as stock is concerned because in a previous mock draft, you actually had the Jets taking Ruben Bain, but in your latest, you had the Jets taking Arval Reese. So I would imagine in your eyes his stock is up. Absolutely. I mean, you talk about somebody at 6'5, 244 lb. He was everything for that Ohio State defense this past season. You could put him at off-ball linebacker, you could put him at edge rusher. He's that jack-of-all-trades player that you can use on the second or even the first level as well. I really love how Matt Patricia used him this last season. He was able to utilize all those tools that he has. So for Darren Moji and Aaron Glenn, I think they're going to fall in love with the skillset of what he has presently, but also what he can be in the future as well. I got to give you a lot of credit because from the get-go, you've always liked Ruben Bain, but in your eyes for the Jets, is his stock falling just a little bit? Just a little bit just because there's more question marks with him just because of the arm length and then he's just not as crafty of a fast rusher like a David Bailey, but I think he's more versatile than the other two in my opinion from a run game perspective and then also how he does rush the passer, but I think it's going to be between David Bailey and Arval Reese at the top of the draft. I still personally believe that Ruben Bain is the best edge rusher in this year's draft just because I have David Bailey as an off-ball linebacker. That's where I believe he should start out personally, but Ruben Bain, if they do select him at two, I'm not going to blink an eye or complain at all, honestly. Where do you stand on Bailey right now? Is he the best Does he have the best technique of all the guys coming out right at this point? From just a pass rush perspective, he obviously is the most productive and you talk about explosiveness out of the starting blocks. I think he's clearly better than the other two in that facet. He still needs to improve a little bit as far as the consistency as a run defender, but I mean, 14 and a half sacks last year, the production speaks for itself. 19 and a half tackles for loss this past season as well. So he's able to get after the quarterback, but he doesn't only create a pressure, but there's a lot of other things that he can do as well. That's why I think if they want somebody that can contribute right away as far as being a 10-plus sack guy even early on as a rookie, I think David Bailey can be that right away. Quickly on the quarterbacks, we talked about Mendoza just a little bit before. Where do you stand on the gap between him and Ty Simpson? I think Mendoza is the clear one in this year's class. He's my undeniable quarterback one at this spot, but Ty Simpson, he got much better early on in the season. Had a little bit of precipitous drop-off at the end, injuries, a lack of run game as well, but that eight-game stretch of where he showed 19 touchdowns, only one interception, a little over 1,700 passing yards as well. He was able to do a lot of things and show a lot of things. Even though he's only a 15-game career starter, I think there's a lot of things to really be intrigued about with Ty from a skillset perspective. This is something that we like to call gate change as far as movement is concerned. For a while now, you've had the Jets looking to move up. We talked to Indy and he said potentially maybe go after a Caleb Downs, but also you've talked about potentially maybe getting a guy like Mekhi Leven. Do you think it makes a lot of sense for the Jets as far as your first round grades are concerned to get out of that 16 spot and go up? I think that's the great thing and goes back to the flexibility that I talked about early on when we were talking. You have 16, you have 33, and you have 44 as well. So if somebody like a Mekhi Leven gets to 12 or 13 or even a Jordan Addison or Carnell Tate, if one of those receivers starts to get in that early teens area, you have two really early second round picks that could really entice a team to potentially trade back. So just imagine Mekhi Leven or Jordan Addison paired with Garrett Wilson. Now you're talking about a dynamic one-two punch. Do you think one of those three make the most sense as a compliment for the Jets when you're talking about a guy like Wilson? I think Garrett Wilson is so good, it doesn't really matter who you have as a number two behind him, but if I had to pick one player to be that number two behind him, it would be Mekhi Leven just because of the slot versatility that he has and I think he can play on the outside as well, but I just think it unlocks another dimension and unlocks another chapter to the playbook as well when you can have somebody that can play outside as well as inside equally as good. So that's why I keep mocking Mekhi Leven to the Jets just because I think it's such a good fit behind Garrett Wilson as that certified wide receiver two. Jordan, let's build a perfect linebacker from this 2026 class using the following five traits: intelligence, football IQ, tackling ability, speed, coverage ability, and motor. So you know this group quite well. Who would you go to as far as intelligence, football IQ? Oh, that's a great question. I would go with Jacob Rodriguez out of Texas Tech. Somebody that is very instinctive. He understands run schemes. You saw, I mean, he was nominated and won pretty much every accolade that he was up for this past season and then just how smart he is as a second level defender. I think he's going to be a really, really good pro. What about coverage ability? Coverage ability, I would go with Sunny Styles in that area just because I mean, somebody that is a former safety, he transitioned to that off-ball linebacker spot and there was no drop-off at all with him. He's so instinctive in coverage. He can really recognize route concepts as well. So I would go with Sunny Styles in that area. How about tackling? Am I able to use the same answer twice because I probably would go with Sunny Styles, but I'll give you a different answer. I'll go with C.J. Allen out of Georgia for that one. Somebody that's a wrap-up finish and very violent tackler when he's stepping downhill. So he's somebody I think potentially could go in that back end of the first round as well, but somebody that is a very violent tackler and can come up and finish ball carriers at the point of attack, I would go with C.J. Allen. How about speed? You know everybody wants a linebacker who can get sideline to sideline. Let's go with um I'm going to cheat here. I'm I have Arval Reese as an off-ball linebacker, so I'm going to use Arval Reese in this situation. He has that sideline-sideline ability. There isn't anything that gets outside of his range when he is playing that off-ball linebacker spot. So Arval Reese would be my contender in this spot. How about motor? You want a guy who never shuts off, who's always got that green light and always on go. That's an easy one for me. It'd be Anthony Hill out of Texas. He's somebody that plays with what I like to call a battery pack in his back and it never loses any notches in the percentage as far as how he plays. He's playing full go at every single opportunity that he gets whether it's moving forward, moving backward, playing against the run, playing against the pass as well. So Anthony Hill, he's another player that is just full go at every single opportunity. So real quickly, that would be an awesome linebacker if you put all those guys together in those traits. Would you consider Styles at two at all with the Jets? And let's say you don't, here's part B the question. Do you think Hill would be a consideration at 33 if you keep that pick? Yeah, I think so. I think that's a great question and I think this is the type of draft of where you throw positional value out of the window and we're seeing guys like a Caleb Downs and Jeremiah Love out of Notre Dame who I think are the two best players in this year's draft being considered as top-10 picks. Just because of the lack of quarterbacks and the lack of blue-chip talent at the top of the draft, it makes sense to consider somebody like a Sunny Styles at number two overall. And if that's the direction the Jets go, I wouldn't be surprised by that at all. Just because he's such a clean evaluation from the tape that he put on this year, the performance that he put on at the combine, and then just the things that he has been able to get better at throughout the season. I think he's such a clean evaluation, and you need that player in the middle. Linebacker's a huge question mark for the Jets right now. So, getting that player in the middle who I've compared to Fred Warner, I don't think anybody's going to complain about taking a Fred Warner type of player at number two overall. Now, on the inverse with Anthony Hill, he's another player I think could be in consideration at number 33 overall, and I think this is a really good linebacker class in general. So, somebody like Anthony Hill that I think is a plug-and-play player, whether it's at middle linebacker or on the weak side, I think you're getting a starter at number 33. If you do go the Anthony Hill route. The Jets have needs at edge, cornerback, receiver, maybe a young quarterback, and offensive line interior. With that being said, let's move to day three of the draft. Can you give us a couple of diamonds, maybe one offensive player and one defensive player, who might make sense for Darren Mougey in the green and white? So, I'll stick with the Jets needs. One player that I think is a diamond in the rough that deserves more love. His name is Kevin Coleman. He's a wide receiver from Missouri, and he's been well-traveled, just like every other player in college football it seems like now. He's transferred three times. Um, he was he actually originally started his career at Jackson State. He was one of Shedur Sanders' very first receivers during their first year at Jackson State. Um, ends up he finishes his career at Missouri, was one of their best targets a season ago. I think he has to transition to the slot on the next level, but very sure-handed, really good route runner. He can run every branch on the route tree. He can climb the ladder and um, get those 50/50 balls over those DBs as well. So, Kevin Coleman definitely would be one player that I definitely would consider. And then another, if the Jets are looking for a cornerback. Now, I think this guy has to be a nickel on the next level, but his name is Jayden Kennedy out of Oregon. Another player that's very instinctive, very physical, has really good ball skills as well. I like those. Uh, how about the quarterback spot? Um, if the Jets don't go early there, and they're looking to take maybe not so much a flyer, but more of a developmental prospect that you like and it might make sense them bringing him in the building. Well, I don't know what how much time we have, but as a former quarterback, I can talk about these guys all day long, especially the very underrated ones. But, somebody that I think is that could carve out a really long career is Luke Altmyer out of Illinois. He's that typical West Coast type of quarterback that gets the ball out really quickly. He's really decisive. He has experience from shotgun and under center. I think he sleep he sees the field really well, and also he has a mobility factor to him as well. So, if they're looking to take somebody in the fifth or the sixth round, and what I like to call lottery tickets, if you're looking to cash in potentially to get one of those late-round lottery tickets, Luke Altmyer out of Illinois is one name that I would be heavily interested in. But, Jordan, why has he been why is Luke been flying under the radar a little bit? I I think it's just because a lot of people see the traits or lack thereof with him, and that was a big reason why like a Brock Purdy fell to the seventh round. Whenever a guy doesn't have those overwhelming traits, and then they don't have a lot of um, year-to-year success as far as putting up the gaudy stats, they're going to be considered a late-round player. But, I was really impressed with him throughout the season, then he goes on. I thought he performed really well at the Senior Bowl as well. He made some nice throws and stacks, some really good days of practices there as well. And he played really good in the game as well. So, you want to see those traits translate especially into an NFL setting like that, and I just think he's continued to check every single box in the process. All right, you've prepared for this because you can wear the GM hat for 32 teams. Now, what I'm going to put the hat on you for the Jets. You got Darren Mougey's spot right now. We're going to do a two-round mock draft with you. Number two overall, who you taking? I'm going to go with Arvell Reese out of Ohio State, and I just think the upside that he has and the potential that he has, whether it's at off-ball linebacker or edge rusher, these are the type of foundational pieces, high-upside pieces that you would love to take with the Jets. And I just think he's just scratching the surface of what he can be. So, I would go with Arvell Reese at number two overall. All right, I'm the commissioner here in the mock draft, and I say Jordan, you can make trades if you want. The Jets do have the number 16 overall pick. So, I'm actually going to uh, stay stand pat here, and Mekhi Wingo is actually on the board just because we're in a hypothetical, and this is our own mock draft, right? So, we make up the rules. So, Mekhi Wingo is sitting there for me at number 16 overall, and I'm running to turn that card in. And I know we have to wait um, for the clock to wind down a little bit on draft day. I know you guys hate that. You want the card to just be turned in, but we're going to make your job easy here, and we're going to turn that card in within a minute of us being on the clock, and I'm going to go with Mekhi Wingo. I just think he's such a great fit alongside Garrett Wilson, and we want to set up um, this infrastructure to where we eventually can welcome in a quarterback. So, just imagine an offensive infrastructure of Olu Fashanu, Alim McNeill at our offensive tackle spots, and then we have Breece Hall in the backfield to complement Mekhi Wingo as well as Garrett Wilson. I think that's such a great setup. All right, Jordan. It is Thursday night. Night one is over, but people are blowing up your phone. You know they want that 33rd overall pick. Are you sitting tight and taking someone? Yeah, I'm going to sit tight, and we're going to take one of the better players who could be available at the top of the draft board. And one name I want Jets fans to become very familiar with is AJ Harris, who is a safety out of LSU. He He's one of my favorite players in this year's draft. You talk about somebody that is an energizer bunny. He brings that type of attitude and intensity that you love to see at the position. And I just love DBs that have a little bit of trash talk to them. And Harris is one of those players that has a lot of confidence. He feels as if he's the best player in the stadium, and it doesn't matter who's in the stadium with him, he's going to feel like he's the best he's the best player there. So, I'm going to go with AJ Harris at number 33 overall. Jets certainly need more takeaways in 2026, and Harris showed a propensity for that on the collegiate level. How about number 44 overall? I'm actually going to go corner here. I think the Jets could use another corner. So, I'm going to go with Brandon Ceaser, who's a corner out of South Carolina. Once again, I don't know if he's going to be here, but this is our mock draft, we make up the rules. Uh, Brandon Ceaser is one player that I'm a big fan of. More athlete than technician right now, but once again, these are the high-upside players that you have time um, to really bank on if you're the Jets. Didn't have any interceptions last season, so he's going to bring some ball production along with him. So, Brandon Ceaser out of South Carolina, I I think he would be a great fit at 44. Finally, Jordan, we're throwing you the virtual whiteboard. You are in the Jets draft room right now. You are a scout, and they're asking you your red star player. Who you standing up for and saying, "This is the guy we need." So, just not basing this on the Jets needs, but just in general, one player that I love is Caleb Downs out of Ohio State. I think he's just such a clean evaluation. He's one of the smartest safeties that I've ever evaluated, and it's very rare to see a player have such [snorts] the high quality of success that he had at two blue-blood programs at Alabama, and then transitioning onto Ohio State. Very sure tackler, he has the ball production that you love to see at the position as well. The player that I compare him to is Budda Baker. We saw Budda Baker, who's going on to be a multi-time all-pro player in Arizona. You can use him in so many different ways. So, I think Aaron Glenn would be really excited to use him in so many different ways. So, Caleb Downs would be my red star player. Jordan, thanks for playing Jets GM just for a day. We're going to continue [music] to follow you, of course, and all your pre-draft analysis on ESPN. [music] Thanks so much. Thank you for having me as always.
